references.text: The Israelites also wept earlier in the wilderness when they complained about the food, showing a pattern of discontent and rebellion against God.
The people grumbled against Moses and Aaron earlier at the Red Sea and in the wilderness, a recurring theme of Israel's complaints.
Moses reminds the Israelites of this event when they grumbled in their tents and refused to enter the land.
The psalmist describes how the people despised the pleasant land and did not believe God's word, but grumbled in their tents.
Paul warns the Corinthians against grumbling as some of the Israelites did, and were killed by the destroyer.
Hebrews refers to this generation as having provoked God through their unbelief and rebellion in the wilderness.
